heroSub: 10 hand-picked Chachoengsao (Paet Riu) hotels we've reviewed in depth — a boutique hotel by the 100-Year-Old Ban Mai Market, a fresh serviced apartment downtown, a Moroccan-style boutique, and a resort on the Bang Pakong River. Prices from about ฿500–1,500/night.
heroStats: ✅ Honest takes from real reviews at every stay
introH2: 🏙️ What types of Chachoengsao hotels are there, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Chachoengsao, which locals usually call Paet Riu, is a secondary city near Bangkok that most people drop by to pay respects to Luang Pho Sothon, stroll the 100-Year-Old Ban Mai Market, and eat well along the Bang Pakong River — so the hotels here don't compete on luxury, but on location, cleanliness, and a vibe that fits your kind of trip. Some are boutique hotels where you sleep above a cafe right by the riverside old market, some are fresh serviced apartments downtown for multi-night stays, some are Moroccan-style buildings you recognize in a glance, and some are resorts on the Bang Pakong River where you wake up to a river view. A lot of people pick the wrong style of stay and feel it wasn't worth it — like coming to make merit but staying far from the temple, or wanting to relax but ending up in a building in the middle of the market. This article rounds up 10 Chachoengsao hotels we've reviewed in depth — across the old-market side, downtown near Wat Sothon, and along the Bang Pakong River — all drawn from reading real guest reviews, telling you both the upsides and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites, with direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Chachoengsao has no metro, but there are several ways to get here. By train, the Eastern Line from Krung Thep Aphiwat or Hua Lamphong station stops at Chachoengsao (Paet Riu) station — cheap fares and good atmosphere, ideal for those who'd rather not drive, and several hotels in this set are within walking distance of the station. By car, it's about an hour-plus from Bangkok and roughly 45–70 min from Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK) into town; every hotel in this article has parking. In town, calling a Grab or hopping on a songthaew is easy. The hotel areas in this article: town center / Na Mueang — near Wat Sothon, the 100-Year-Old Ban Mai Market, and the train station, easy to explore on foot; Bang Pakong riverside (Khlong Na) — quiet resorts that need a 10–15 min drive into town; Bang Pakong / Wellgrow Industrial Estate — handy for those working in the estate, closer to the airport than the town center.

entries.type: Boutique Hotel + Cafe, 3-Star · By the Old Market
entries.name: The Brown House Hotel
entries.badge: ☕ Sleep above a cafe, by the 100-Year-Old Market
entries.mrtTag: 📍 By the 100-Year-Old Ban Mai Market · on the Bang Pakong River
entries.addr: 556, 558 Supakit Road, Na Mueang, Mueang Chachoengsao District
entries.storyHtml: If you ask which Chachoengsao hotel cafe lovers and old-market fans keep recommending to each other, many reviews put The Brown House Hotel first every time — a small boutique hotel of about 12 rooms in an old shophouse that's been renovated anew, painted in warm browns and dressed up in a floral English-cottage style, with a cafe and dessert shop on the ground floor and the rooms upstairs. What makes people fall for it is the location: right by the 100-Year-Old Ban Mai Market on the Bang Pakong River — step out the door and within a few paces you reach the old market, shrines, and riverside restaurants — and stays this close to the actual market are rare. Another charm is sleeping above the cafe and heading down in the morning for coffee and freshly baked pastries before the market gets busy. The room people photograph and talk about most is the one facing the Bang Pakong River; some have a balcony to sit and watch the water and the sunset, which many name as their main reason for staying here. From real reviews, the cleanliness score sits high at around 9.0, many say the rooms are roomier than expected and the beds soft and comfy, and the breakfast — cooked fresh to order, from flower-shaped bread and shrimp congee to an American breakfast — gets praise in nearly every review. Honest caveats from the reviews: the building has several floors but no elevator, so you walk the stairs; it's on the road and near the railway, so some rooms catch traffic and train noise; the cafe closes fairly early around 5 p.m.; and river-view rooms are limited and need to be booked ahead. Best for couples, small families, and cafe lovers who want to explore the old market and stay riverside with atmosphere, rather than those hunting for a resort with a pool.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want a river view with a balcony, book the Riverview Room well ahead because they're limited. If you're traveling with elderly guests or heavy luggage, ask for a ground-floor room first since there's no elevator. And order the main dish of your breakfast the night before, since the kitchen cooks each plate fresh.
pros: Location right by the 100-Year-Old Ban Mai Market — stroll the market and shrines on foot
Sleep above the cafe, decorated in a cute cottage style, thoughtful in every corner
Riverside rooms with sunset views over the Bang Pakong River · rooms are roomy and clean
Breakfast made fresh and tasty, attentive staff (from the reviews)
cons: Building has several floors but no elevator, so you walk the stairs
On the road and near the railway; some rooms catch car/train noise
Cafe closes early around 5 p.m. · river-view rooms are limited, book ahead

entries.type: Small In-Town Hotel, 2-Star · Near Wat Sothon
entries.name: Sunee View Hotel
entries.badge: 🛕 Walk to Wat Sothon · best value for merit-makers
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sothon · about 1 km from Wat Sothon, walkable
entries.addr: 58/59 Soi 7, Thep Khunakon Road, Sothon, Mueang Chachoengsao District
entries.storyHtml: If you're coming to Chachoengsao mainly to pay respects to Luang Pho Sothon, Sunee View Hotel is a name that hits the mark for merit-makers and budget travelers — a small hotel in Sothon subdistrict, only about 1 kilometer from Wat Sothon Wararam Worawihan, close enough to walk over for morning prayers, which is very near compared with many hotels in the province that need a multi-kilometer drive. The hotel sits on a quiet soi, so the atmosphere is calmer than hotels on the main road, and there's a sitting garden and outdoor space to step out for fresh air, giving a private feel. The main rooms are Deluxe Studios with a king bed and air-con, a window for natural light, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, and a private bathroom; some have a balcony overlooking the garden. From real reviews, the points that draw consistent praise are the location near the temple, the quiet that makes for easy sleep, clean rooms, and friendly, helpful staff; many say the hot water works well and the water pressure is good. There are also small touches you don't often find at this price — bike rental and a fishing corner — plus free parking, free Wi-Fi, and a 24-hour counter, with staff who speak both Thai and English. Honest caveats from the reviews: the bed is fairly firm for some (though you can ask for an extra topper); there's no pool or resort-style facilities; the hotel is on a soi that can be a little hard to find the first time; and the surrounding shops aren't dense, so you'll drive into town if you want more food options. Best for elderly travelers and merit-making families, business visitors, and road-tripping drivers looking for a budget stay as close to the temple as possible.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Make the most of the roughly 1-kilometer distance — head out early on foot or a short drive to pay respects to Luang Pho Sothon before the crowds. If you like a soft bed, ask for an extra topper at check-in. And if you want a room with a balcony, specify it when booking since not every room has one.
pros: Location near Wat Sothon, about 1 km — walk over for prayers — the number-one selling point
Quiet, calm atmosphere with a sitting garden, easy sleep
Very budget-friendly from about ฿550 · free parking and Wi-Fi
Friendly, kind, helpful staff · bikes and a fishing spot
cons: Bed is fairly firm for some (extra topper available)
No pool or resort-style facilities
On a soi, can be hard to find the first time · surrounding shops aren't dense

entries.name: Yenjit Resort
entries.badge: 🌳 #1 in Chachoengsao · leafy, near the train station
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Na Mueang · about 200 m from the train station, 9 min walk
tags: 🚉 Walk to the train station ~9 min
entries.addr: 247/40 Maha Chakkraphat Road, Na Mueang, Mueang Chachoengsao District
entries.storyHtml: Among Chachoengsao hotels, if you measure by score and ranking, Yenjit Resort (officially Yenjit Bungalow and Resort) is the top performer in this set — Tripadvisor ranks it #1 of 6 hotels in Chachoengsao, and it scores 8.9 from 30 reviews on Trip.com. What sets it apart is how well it pulls off being downtown yet leafy: a resort of bungalows and low-rise buildings tucked into a soi in the town center, under big shade trees that keep it cooler and quieter than many expect. Open since 2013 with about 60 rooms, its biggest advantage is the location — only about 200 meters from Chachoengsao train station, roughly a 9-minute walk — so for anyone taking the train from Bangkok to Paet Riu, a location like this is hard to match: step off the train and wheel your bags straight to the hotel. From real reviews, the most consistent praise goes to the leafy atmosphere that feels like a tucked-away corner in the middle of town, rooms that are roomy and clean, friendly owner and staff, and — singled out especially — the free breakfast buffet that's better than expected and changes its menu every day, with savory dishes, sweets, and fruit. There's also free parking with an EV charging point, plus a fitness room. Honest caveats from the reviews: the soi entrance is fairly narrow, with cars sometimes passing one at a time, so drivers of larger vehicles or newer drivers should ease in; and there's no pool and no all-day restaurant. Beyond the entrance, there are barely any significant negative reviews. Best for travelers arriving by train, business visitors or those paying respects to Luang Pho Sothon, and anyone who likes a quiet, leafy resort feel on an easy budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Arriving by train is the best value, since you can walk from the station straight to the hotel, saving both fare and time. If you drive, allow for the narrow soi entrance and ease in slowly. And don't miss the free breakfast buffet served 07:00–10:00, which is a highlight here.
pros: TripAdvisor #1 in Chachoengsao · score 8.9 from real reviews
About 200 meters' walk to the train station — most convenient by train
Leafy atmosphere with lots of trees, quiet and calm · rooms roomy and clean
Free breakfast buffet done well, menu changes daily · EV charging
cons: Soi entrance is fairly narrow, cars sometimes pass one at a time
No pool and no all-day restaurant
Prices rise during festivals and the Wat Sothon fair, book ahead

entries.name: Malone Maranatha
entries.revCount: Real reviews about 8.0 · TripAdvisor about 4/5 · #2 boutique in town
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sothon Phatthana Rd, Soi 2 · near Wat Sothon and Robinson
entries.addr: 99/5 Moo 2, Sothon Phatthana Rd, Soi 2, Sothon, Mueang Chachoengsao District
entries.storyHtml: If you drive along Sothon Phatthana Road in Chachoengsao and a brightly colored building with rounded shapes — unlike anything you've seen in Paet Riu before — catches your eye, that's Malone Maranatha — a small boutique hotel selling itself as the province's only Arabian-Moroccan building, built of brick, stone, sand, and metal and decorated in bright colors inside and out until it has become a small landmark of the area. What sets it apart from hotels at the same price is that it leans on character as its selling point rather than competing on facilities — a stay that's memorable because it looks like nothing else in town. It sits on Sothon Phatthana Road, Soi 2, about 3.5 kilometers from the town center, around 5–10 minutes' drive from Wat Sothon, and near Robinson department store for a walk-over food run. With about 24–25 rooms — Deluxe Double, Superior Double, and Superior Twin — all air-conditioned and non-smoking, with a fridge, LCD TV, and free instant coffee, the decor borrows Moroccan colors and patterns to give the rooms character. From real reviews, the consistent praise is that the building is striking and photogenic from many angles, the rooms look new and clean, the beds are comfortable, and the staff are friendly and attentive; the picnic lawn and BBQ area are a bonus you rarely get at this price. Tripadvisor ranks it #2 of 8 boutique-type stays in Mueang district. Honest caveats from the reviews: there's no pool or gym; the area around the hotel is fairly quiet and shops aren't dense, so a late-night meal means driving into town or ordering delivery; and some older reviews mention that windows in certain rooms don't open easily, owing to the building's design. Best for business visitors, those paying respects at Wat Sothon, or anyone stopping over in town who wants a clean, new-looking room with a distinctive vibe at an affordable price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Use it as a base to pay respects at Wat Sothon in the morning before the crowds, since it's about 5–10 minutes' drive away. Check clearly whether the rate you book includes an English breakfast, as some packages add a charge. And if you like opening the window for natural air, ask about it or view the room first.
pros: The town's only Moroccan-style building, distinctive and photogenic from many angles
Rooms look new and clean, beds comfortable · affordable price
Near Wat Sothon and Robinson department store, easy to get around town
Picnic lawn / BBQ area · free Wi-Fi and parking
cons: No pool or gym
Area around the hotel is fairly quiet, shops not dense
Windows in some rooms don't open easily, owing to the building's design (from reviews)

entries.name: JK Living Hotel & Service Apartment
entries.badge: 🏙️ Highest score in the set · fresh, roomy rooms
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pracha Sawan Road, Na Mueang · near Wat Sothon-industrial estate
tags: 🚲 Bikes to borrow · monthly stays available
entries.addr: 72/3-4 Pracha Sawan Road, Na Mueang, Mueang Chachoengsao District
entries.storyHtml: If you're coming to Paet Riu for a longer stretch — working in the industrial estate, here for several days of business, or just wanting a room roomier than a standard hotel at a friendly price — JK Living Hotel And Service Apartment is the name leading on review scores in town, and it's the highest-scoring stay in this article at 9.2 from 42 reviews. What sets it apart from typical small hotels is that it's a serviced-apartment-meets-hotel designed for actually living in, not just a one-night crash. Opened in 2016 with about 44 rooms, it sits on Pracha Sawan Road right in the town center. What guests praise most is that the rooms are new, very clean, and roomier than typical hotel rooms at the same price, with space to set things down and a desk to work or eat at; many reviews mention the large fridge that fits plenty, ideal for long stays. The location stands out too, since you can drive to Wat Sothon Wararam in about 3 minutes and it's within driving range of the industrial-estate area — handy for those who go in and out of the factory daily but don't want to stay in the estate, where it's quiet and food is hard to find. There's an in-house fitness room, free bikes to borrow, a cafe praised for its coffee, and free private parking, accepting both daily and monthly stays. The service score reaches around 9.4, which is very high — the staff are friendly and helpful. Honest caveats from the reviews: there's no pool and no nature views since it's a downtown apartment; breakfast is light, with coffee, tea, and bread; Wi-Fi registration at some points is in Thai, which trips up foreign guests; and some rooms face the road and may catch noise from outside. Best for those working in the industrial estate, here for long business trips, or paying respects to Luang Pho Sothon and wanting to stay several days in a roomy, good-value room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're working in the estate or staying long, ask the hotel directly about weekly or monthly rates — they're often better than stacking up daily bookings. If you're a light sleeper, ask for a room away from the road. And if you're a foreign guest, ask staff to help set up the Wi-Fi at check-in.
pros: Highest score in the article 9.2 · service and cleanliness scores very high
Rooms new, very clean, roomier than typical hotel rooms at the same price
3-minute drive to Wat Sothon and near the industrial estate · monthly stays available
Free parking, fitness room and bikes to borrow, good for multi-night stays
cons: No pool, leans practical over nature views
Light breakfast with few options, full breakfast costs extra
Some rooms face the road, may catch noise · Wi-Fi registration at some points is in Thai

entries.name: Kesorn Boutique
entries.badge: 🧼 Cleaner and quieter than the price suggests · budget
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Suk Prayun Road, Na Mueang · about 2 km from Wat Sothon
tags: 🧼 Rooms cleaner than the price suggests
🙏 A few minutes' drive to Wat Sothon
entries.addr: 147/6 Suk Prayun Road, Na Mueang, Mueang Chachoengsao District
entries.storyHtml: If you're in Paet Riu on an easy budget and want a small stay that's clean, quiet, and easy to park at downtown, Kesorn Boutique Residence at 8 Riew is a name budget travelers in Chachoengsao often run into — a boutique guesthouse of about 33 rooms that plays it smart by being a small place that keeps room quality more in check than many older hotels in town that let their rooms run down over time. The main selling point is that it does the basics well — cleanliness and quiet — the two things budget guests weigh most. Many reviews say roughly that they didn't expect much because of the low price, but were surprised on entering the room that it was cleaner and tidier than expected. It sits on Suk Prayun Road in Na Mueang subdistrict, about 2 kilometers from Wat Sothon Wararam — a few minutes' drive away — and within easy reach of the town center, the 100-Year-Old Ban Mai Market, and the Bang Pakong riverside. There are several room types, from knockdown rooms starting at ฿550 to Standard Double and Standard Twin rooms of about 20 sq m with windows and a more open feel; every room has air-con, a flat-screen TV, and an en-suite bathroom with a hot shower. There's free parking, which guests mention most positively. Honest caveats from the reviews: some of the cheaper knockdown rooms have no window, which feels stuffy and sometimes musty; some nights there's dog noise in the neighborhood; there's no elevator, so upstairs rooms mean walking up; and some items like a hair dryer need to be requested. Best for budget travelers paying respects to Luang Pho Sothon, driving through town, or here for a short errand who want a clean, quiet room in the few-hundred-baht range — just book a room with a window first.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Always pick a room with a window first; if your budget allows, skip the cheapest knockdown room and choose a Standard, which is more open and cuts the musty smell. Driving yourself is the best value since there's free parking and a quick drive to the temple. And if you find it hard to sleep, ask for an inner room and bring earplugs in case of neighborhood dog noise.
pros: Rooms clean and tidy, beyond the price at the few-hundred-baht level
Quiet at night, easy sleep, no road noise
Free private parking · quick drive to Wat Sothon and the town center
Staff look after you well, as small stays do · friendly price
cons: Some cheaper knockdown rooms have no window · some rooms are musty
Some nights there's dog noise in the neighborhood
No elevator, and some items like a hair dryer need to be requested

entries.name: Siri Sothorn Apartment
entries.badge: 🙏 In-town location, 6-minute drive to Wat Sothon
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chachoengsao-Bang Pakong Road, Na Mueang · in town
entries.addr: 672/5 Chachoengsao-Bang Pakong Road, Na Mueang, Mueang Chachoengsao District
entries.storyHtml: If you're after a budget stay in the town center of Paet Riu that's a few minutes' drive from paying respects to Luang Pho Sothon, Siri Sothorn Apartment is a name that comes up often on booking platforms — a rental-apartment-style stay that sells on location and price more than luxury or newness. Its clearest strength is the location: on Chachoengsao-Bang Pakong Road, only about 1.3 kilometers from the town center and roughly a 6-minute drive to Wat Sothon Wararam Worawihan, about 2.8 kilometers from the train station, with easy access into town, to the market, and to the major temples. It's an apartment-style stay where many rooms have a fridge, a kettle, and a private balcony or terrace to step out for fresh air or hang laundry, suited to longer stays, with something you don't often find at this price — a fitness room — plus free private parking and a 24-hour front desk. From real reviews, the praise side is the in-town location with a quick drive to the temple and into town, a friendly price, and staff who communicate well and warmly. But to be straight, it's a building of a fair age, so the reviews clearly split two ways. Honest caveats from the reviews: the building and rooms are aged; some rooms feel musty with wear on the furniture; there's no breakfast and no in-house restaurant; and rooms facing the main road catch some traffic noise. Because rooms vary in condition, many reviews say that if you get a room you don't like, asking to switch makes it better. Best for budget travelers who want an in-town location, free parking, and an apartment-style room with a fridge for short-to-medium stays — as long as you set expectations to a budget in-town stay, not one focused on newness.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Because rooms vary in condition, if you check in and get a room that's musty or older than expected, don't hesitate to ask to view a room or switch. The stay has no breakfast, so plan your morning meal or buy food to keep in the fridge. And if you're a light sleeper, ask for a room not facing the road.
pros: In-town location, 6-minute drive to Wat Sothon, quick into town
Budget-friendly price · free private parking and a fitness room
Apartment-style rooms with a fridge, kettle, and some with a balcony
Staff communicate well, friendly · 24-hour front desk
cons: Building and rooms are aged, some rooms musty with wear
No breakfast and no in-house restaurant
Rooms facing the main road catch some traffic noise (from reviews)

entries.name: The Chill Classic House
entries.revCount: Real reviews about 7.3 · TripAdvisor about 4.1/5 · #1 specialty lodging
entries.badge: 🎨 Arty and photogenic · walk from the train station
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Maha Chakkraphat Road · about 900 m from the train station
entries.addr: 191/45-46 Maha Chakkraphat Road, Na Mueang, Mueang Chachoengsao District
entries.storyHtml: If you want a Chachoengsao stay you can walk to within minutes of stepping off the train, where you wake up to free morning coffee at the ground-floor cafe, at a very easy price, The Chill Classic House is a small boutique guesthouse that budget travelers and those who come without driving keep recommending — a renovated four-story shophouse done in a classic-arty tone, brightly decorated unlike a typical shophouse, with a signature world-map photo corner, a cafe and lounge with a ping-pong table on the ground floor, and about 12 rooms upstairs. It opened in late 2019. What makes it memorable is the decor, which many reviews describe as arty and chic for the walls, furniture, and decorative pieces clearly put together with thought. Its top strength is the location — only about 900 meters, or a 10–15 minute walk, from Chachoengsao (Paet Riu) train station — so those taking the train from Bangkok can wheel their bags over on foot; there are restaurants within 100 meters, a 7-Eleven nearby, and songthaews at the mouth of the soi, while the 100-Year-Old Ban Mai Market and Wat Sothon are about 1 kilometer away. From real reviews, guests praise the comfortable beds, the cold air-con, the fast Wi-Fi, the fresh decor, the photogenic world-map corner, the friendly staff, and the value for money; many foreign reviews call it excellent value. Honest caveats from the reviews: some rooms have a musty smell when you open the door; the hot water is sometimes inconsistent; the building has several floors but no elevator, so you walk the stairs; and some details on the booking page, such as breakfast, may not fully match reality. Best for solo travelers, backpackers, couples, and those taking the train to Paet Riu without driving, who want a cutely decorated, budget stay as a base for visiting temples and the old market.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Arriving by train and walking over is the best advantage, since there are songthaews and a 7-Eleven nearby. If you're sensitive to noise or smell, ask for an inner room and run the air-con to air it out for a while after entering. And if breakfast matters, ask about the package before booking, since some reviews felt the listed details didn't match reality exactly.
pros: Location near Paet Riu train station, about 900 meters — easy to arrive without driving
Classic-arty decor, photogenic, with a world-map corner
Comfortable beds, cold air-con, fast Wi-Fi · great value
Ground-floor cafe with free morning coffee and a ping-pong table, friendly staff
cons: Some rooms have a musty smell when you open the door
Hot water is sometimes inconsistent · no elevator, you walk the stairs
Some breakfast/view details on the booking page don't fully match reality

entries.name: Suntara Wellness Resort
entries.badge: 🌊 On the Bang Pakong River · big family pool
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khlong Na, on the Bang Pakong River · 10 min to Wat Sothon
entries.addr: 5/2 Moo 1, Khlong Na, Mueang Chachoengsao District
entries.storyHtml: If you want a Chachoengsao stay where you sip coffee by the Bang Pakong River in the evening and watch the sunset turn the sky, in a quiet resort setting rather than a building in the middle of the market, Suntara Wellness Resort & Hotel is the name people who pay respects to Luang Pho Sothon and then want to stay riverside tend to think of — a 4-star wellness resort on the Bang Pakong River on the Khlong Na subdistrict side, the quieter and more natural side than the market side. Stays that genuinely face the Bang Pakong River in Chachoengsao aren't many, and Suntara is one of the few where many rooms and the upper floors get a full river view, especially in the morning and evening as the light hits the water. The most-mentioned highlight is the large outdoor pool with a separate kids' pool that families with children love most; many reviews praise it as big and clean. As a wellness resort it also has a spa and massage, fitness, karaoke, a riverside bar, and bikes to ride along the river, plus 2 restaurants and a fresh-cooked breakfast that many guests praise. The location is good too — only about 10 minutes' drive from Wat Sothon Wararam, so you can head out early for prayers and come back to swim and relax in a single day — and about 50–60 minutes from Suvarnabhumi Airport. Honest caveats from the reviews: the building is getting on in age, some rooms look dated and a few air-con units are noisy; during renovation periods some guests encountered paint smell and dust; some staff have limited English; and the location is fairly quiet, with no convenience store or restaurant within walking distance, so it suits those who drive themselves. Best for families bringing kids to swim, couples wanting a quiet riverside stay, and those set on paying respects to Luang Pho Sothon and then finding a riverside spot to relax.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Specify a river-facing room on an upper floor when booking, since not every room sees the water and upper-floor rooms look out farther across the river. If you're concerned about room condition, ask for a recently renovated room and check whether there's construction during your stay. And if you don't have a car, bring food along, since the area around the resort is quiet.
pros: Beautiful full Bang Pakong River views, especially in the evening in rooms facing the right way
Big pool and kids' pool, great for families bringing children to swim
Has a spa, fitness, karaoke, and fresh-cooked breakfast that earns praise
Quiet and private, about 10 minutes from Wat Luang Pho Sothon
cons: Building is getting on in age, some rooms look dated and air-con is noisy
Some renovation periods have paint smell and dust (from reviews)
Surroundings are quiet, no convenience store within walking distance · inconvenient without a car

entries.type: Budget Hotel, 2-Star · New Building, Near Industrial Estate
entries.name: Wellgrow Service House
entries.badge: ✨ New 2025 building · cleanest in the set
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Near Wellgrow Industrial Estate · Phimpha, Bang Pakong District
entries.addr: Near Wellgrow Industrial Estate, Phimpha, Bang Pakong District, Chachoengsao
entries.storyHtml: If you have to work or run errands around Wellgrow Industrial Estate in Bang Pakong district, or you're driving this route and want to stop for a night at an inexpensive price, Wellgrow Service House is a new stay leading on review scores in this area — a budget hotel in a new building that just opened in 2025, so everything is still brand new, from the walls and floors to the in-room furniture. It was built specifically to serve workers and pass-through drivers in the Bang Pakong area, focused on one thing: a clean, comfortable sleep at an inexpensive budget. Its first strength is the location, so close to Wellgrow Industrial Estate you barely need to allow travel time to work — a big advantage for early shifts or night shifts — with easy access to the main road; and what many like is that it's only about 45 minutes' drive from Suvarnabhumi Airport. There are several room types, from Standard King with a garden view to the roomier Signature Room and Deluxe Single Premium, all decorated in a bright, modern tone with air-con, a flat-screen TV, a work desk, a rain shower, and free Wi-Fi. From real reviews, the most consistent praise is that the rooms are new and very clean, the bed is soft, the duvet warm, and it's quiet at night for easy sleep; the cleanliness score reaches around 9.7 and the service score about 9.4, numbers that are very hard to find in a few-hundred-baht stay, plus free parking and an elevator. Honest caveats from the reviews: there's no breakfast and restaurants around are hard to find, needing about a 5–7 minute drive (so it suits those with a car); some navigation apps lead to the wrong spot; being near the road and rice fields, some nights bring insects and a bit of traffic noise; and the in-room amenities are basic. Best for those working in Wellgrow Industrial Estate and drivers passing through the Bang Pakong area who want a clean, quiet new room with free parking on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If it's your first time, call the hotel to check the route or watch the signs carefully, since some apps lead to the wrong spot. Bring food and drinking water in advance, especially if you don't have a car, since shops around need a 5–7 minute drive. And have a deposit of about ฿300 ready at check-in.

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates from the standard-room range and may change by date and season; we recommend checking the real price and comparing 3 sites before every booking. The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms, not from staying ourselves. During the Luang Pho Sothon worship fair and long holidays, hotels in the Chachoengsao town center fill up fast and prices rise, so book ahead and choose free-cancellation options if your plans aren't firm. Chachoengsao has no metro — come by the Eastern Line train from Bangkok or drive about an hour-plus; it's roughly 45–70 minutes from Suvarnabhumi Airport into town. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — Common Questions Travelers Ask About Chachoengsao Hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best Chachoengsao hotel?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. By review score, JK Living Hotel & Service Apartment is highest in the article at 9.2, a serviced apartment with fresh, roomy rooms downtown. By ranking, Yenjit Resort is TripAdvisor #1 in Chachoengsao, leafy and near the train station. For an old-market cafe vibe, The Brown House Hotel. For a riverside stay, Suntara Wellness Resort. And for the cleanest new room on a budget, Wellgrow Service House, a new 2025 building.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Chachoengsao hotels cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start at about ฿500–1,500 per night. The most budget side is The Chill Classic House from ฿500, Sunee View and Kesorn Boutique from ฿550, Siri Sothorn from ฿590. Mid-range is Malone Maranatha and Wellgrow from ฿700, Yenjit from ฿800, JK Living from ฿806. And the top side is Suntara on the river from ฿1,400 and The Brown House from ฿1,500. All prices are approximate starting rates from standard rooms; festival periods may run higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ Which Chachoengsao hotel is good and near Wat Sothon?
faq.a: The closest, walkable to Wat Sothon, is Sunee View Hotel, about 1 kilometer away. A short drive away are JK Living at about 3 minutes, Kesorn Boutique at about 2 kilometers, Siri Sothorn at about 6 minutes, and Malone Maranatha at about 5–10 minutes. And Suntara Wellness Resort on the river is about 10 minutes' drive away, good for those who want to pay respects and then relax riverside.

faq.q: ❓ Which Chachoengsao hotel can you walk to from the train station?
faq.a: Chachoengsao is a city you can conveniently visit by the Eastern Line train from Bangkok. The hotels walkable from the train station are Yenjit Resort, about 200 meters away, a 9-minute walk (TripAdvisor #1), and The Chill Classic House, about 900 meters away, a 10–15 minute walk, with arty decor. Both suit those who come without driving much.

faq.q: ❓ Are there Chachoengsao hotels on the Bang Pakong River?
faq.a: Yes, but not many. In this article, Suntara Wellness Resort is a 4-star wellness resort on the Bang Pakong River in the Khlong Na area, where many rooms and the upper floors face the river with views of the water and the sunset, with a big pool and kids' pool, from ฿1,400. And The Brown House Hotel in town also has riverside rooms facing the Bang Pakong River with sunset views from the balcony, from ฿1,500, right by the 100-Year-Old Ban Mai Market.

faq.q: ❓ Which Chachoengsao hotel is good and near the industrial estate?
faq.a: If you're working in the estate around Bang Pakong, Wellgrow Service House is closest to Wellgrow Industrial Estate, a new 2025 building with very clean rooms from ฿700, about 45 minutes from Suvarnabhumi Airport. If you'd rather stay in town and drive to the estate, JK Living Hotel & Service Apartment is a serviced apartment with monthly stays available and roomy rooms from ฿806. Both have free parking and suit those who drive themselves.
